                                     PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                         § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                      §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                   §            OF TEXAS


                      COMMENTS OF WISE ENERGY RESOURCES

       COMES NOW Wise Energy Resources (Wise) and files these comments regarding

Commission Staff’s Discussion Draft proposing a new 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC)

§25.194 relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards, which would set forth the standards

and criteria for an electric utility to interconnect a large load customer to the ERCOT transmission

network. Commission Staff requested comments be filed by December 19, 2025, so these

comments are timely filed.

       Wise Energy Resources owns over 3 GW of large load projects which have been under

active development since 2023 in ERCOT North and Houston Zones. Wise affiliates own over

200,000 acres, with much of that acreage located in the Permian Basin.


                     COMMENTS ON STAFF’S DISCUSSION DRAFT

       Wise recommends Commission consideration of two issues in the Discussion Draft: 1)

clarifying the extent to which this new rule will apply to projects for which interconnection has

already been requested and studies are in process; and 2) deleting the “but for” test related to

contribution in aid to construction (CIAC).

The Commission Should Clarify Application of the Rule to Large Load Projects Already Under
Review.

       Wise acknowledges that the significant financial security required in subsection (e) will

provide additional clarity regarding which projects and developers are real and which are

speculative, an issue that needs to be addressed with the continually increasing large load queue.
 However, there is a lack of clarity in the Staff’s Discussion Draft regarding how adoption of the

new rule would impact large load customers that already are in the process of electric utility

interconnection studies and/or ERCOT studies. Application of the rule to these entities should be

clarified so that large load customers that already have invested millions of dollars in the

interconnection process are not subjected to new requirements retroactively that require the

customers to repeat an earlier stage of the interconnection process they have already completed or

have underway. However, the financial security provisions of the new rule still could be applied

to these large load customers.

Contribution in Aid of Construction “but for” Test May Be Too Broad.

       Paragraph (h)(9) of the Staff’s Discussion Draft sets forth the parameters for the CIAC to

be paid by the large load customer to cover costs that are directly attributable to interconnecting

the customer. Wise’s concern is with the "but for" test in subparagraph (B), starting at page 20,

line 19 in the Staff’s Discussion Draft. Simply stated, this could be read overly broad. While the

concept that the large load customer needs to pay for the transmission upgrades that are directly

attributed to them is reasonable, the "but for" test has the potential to subject a large load customer

to much broader liability for the cost of upgrades that also benefit other customers on the ERCOT

grid as a whole. To address this concern, Wise suggests deleting subsection (h)(9)(B).




                                                                                                     2
                                           CONCLUSION

       Wise appreciates the opportunity to submit these comments and encourages the

Commission to move to formal publication of a proposed rule consistent with these comments.


                                                  Respectfully submitted,

                                                  /s/ Grant Huber
                                                  Director of Energy & Industrials
                                                  Wise Energy Resources
                                                  6851 NE Loop 820
                                                  North Richland Hills, TX 76110
                                                  grant.huber@wiseadv.com
                                                  (847) 727-9163


                                                  December 19, 2025

                                    PROJECT NO. 58481

RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                       § PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                    §
STANDARDS UNDER PURA §37.0561                 §            OF TEXAS


                    COMMENTS OF WISE ENERGY RESOURCES

                                EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 •   Application of the new rule to projects for which interconnection has already been
     requested and studies are in process should be clarified. Large load customers that already
     have invested millions of dollars in the interconnection process should not be subjected to
     new requirements retroactively that require the customers to repeat an earlier stage of the
     interconnection process they have already completed or have underway. However, the
     financial security provisions of the new rule still could be applied to these large load
     customers.

 •   Regarding CIAC in (h)(9)(B), the "but for" test has the potential to subject a data center to
     much broader liability for the cost of upgrades that also benefit ERCOT customers as a
     whole. To address this concern, Wise suggests deleting subsection (h)(9)(B).
